Manually unroll the small fixed number of iterations.
Split helpers so calls form a directed acyclic graph.
canonical_fix: Remove the recursive bpf2bpf call and express the repeated work as a verifier-bounded loop or as an acyclic/unrolled call sequence.
expected_explanation: helper_a contains a bpf2bpf call to itself, creating a recursive subprogram call graph. The verifier requires an acyclic finite call graph even if the source-level branch appears bounded.
model_answer:
The verifier rejects this before normal instruction/range analysis because the subprogram call graph contains a direct cycle:

```text
entry -> helper_a
helper_a -> helper_a
```

Even though the source appears to bound the recursion with:

```asm
r1 += 1;
if r1 < 4 goto l0;
```

the verifier does not allow recursive bpf-to-bpf calls at all. It requires the subprogram call graph to be acyclic so stack depth and analysis remain bounded.

The smallest source-level fix is to rewrite the self-call as an explicit bounded loop inside `helper_a`. The logic is equivalent for the current program: starting with `r1 = 0`, increment `r1` until it reaches `4`, then return.

Patch:

```diff
diff --git a/case.c b/case.c
index 0000000..0000000 100644
--- a/case.c
+++ b/case.c
@@ -13,12 +13,11 @@ static __naked __noinline __attribute__((used))
 void helper_a(void)
 {
 	asm volatile ("					\
+l0_%=:							\
 	r1 += 1;					\
 	r0 = r1;					\
 	if r1 < 4 goto l0_%=;				\
 	exit;						\
-l0_%=:	call helper_a;					\
-	exit;						\
 "	::: __clobber_all);
 }
```

After this change, `helper_a` no longer contains a bpf-to-bpf call to itself, so the call graph is acyclic. The verifier should then analyze the backward jump as a bounded loop: `r1` is incremented each iteration and the loop exits once `r1 >= 4`.

A bounded loop or acyclic rewrite is needed
